scheme_name: Green Credit Programme (GCP) and Indian Carbon Market
target_beneficiary: Farmers, Farmer-Producer Organizations (FPOs), cooperatives, private sector entities, and any individual or organization undertaking environmental activities
benefit_details: Earn tradable green credits and carbon credits for adopting positive environmental actions. Income generated by selling verified credits to entities needing to offset their emissions. Key earning activities for farmers include zero tillage farming, direct seeded rice (DSR), agroforestry and tree plantation, avoiding stubble burning, adopting organic and natural farming practices, water conservation and rainwater harvesting, and soil organic carbon enhancement. Note: this scheme is newer and less standardized than the others in this dataset — exact payout amounts per credit are not fixed nationally and depend on the aggregator/market; avoid quoting specific rupee figures per credit unless independently confirmed.
eligibility_criteria: Must adopt verifiable regenerative agricultural or environmental practices that increase soil organic matter and carbon sequestration. Individual farmers usually participate through aggregators, FPOs, or cooperatives rather than individually. Projects must pass Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) standards.
how_to_apply: Register environmental projects on the official GCP portal (moefcc-gcp.in). For carbon credits, farmers typically join projects through FPOs, cooperatives, or specialized agri-tech partners and aggregators who handle the MRV process. Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) manages the Indian Carbon Market framework.
documents_required: Land records, aggregator or FPO membership agreement, MRV (Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification) data and documentation. Specific requirements vary by project type and aggregator.
contact_details: GCP Portal: moefcc-gcp.in. BEE Portal: beeindia.gov.in. Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) formulates targets and MRV standards. Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education (ICFRE) administers green credits.

target_beneficiary: Individual farmers, SHGs, FPOs, JLGs, and private entrepreneurs setting up livestock and fodder enterprises
benefit_details: 50% capital subsidy (up to Rs 25 lakh for goat/sheep breeding farms of 100-500 animals; up to Rs 25 lakh for poultry breeding units; up to Rs 30 lakh for pig breeding units; and up to Rs 50 lakh for fodder seed production units). Balance financed by bank loan and entrepreneur contribution.
eligibility_criteria: Individuals or groups with land ownership/lease suitable for animal sheds and fodder cultivation. Must possess basic livestock management experience or training.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the National Livestock Mission Portal at nlm.udyamimitra.in. Application is evaluated by State Level Executive Committee (SLEC) and scheduled lending bank.
documents_required: Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, Land ownership/lease documents, Project report/estimates, Training certificate in animal husbandry (if available).
contact_details: Portal: nlm.udyamimitra.in. Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD).

target_beneficiary: Fishers, fish farmers, fish workers, SHGs, JLGs, and fisheries cooperatives
benefit_details: Financial assistance of 40% of project cost for General Category and 60% for SC/ST and Women beneficiaries for aquaculture pond construction, biofloc units, recirculatory aquaculture systems (RAS), motorized fishing boats, cages in reservoirs, and cold chain transport vehicles.
eligibility_criteria: Fishers and rural youth having access to water bodies, land suitable for pond construction, or active registration with State Fisheries Department.
how_to_apply: Submit project proposal online at pmmsy.dof.gov.in or directly submit physical application to District Fisheries Office / District Level Committee (DLC).
documents_required: Aadhaar Card, Land/Water body lease or ownership documents, Caste certificate (for 60% subsidy), Bank passbook details, Detailed project estimate.
contact_details: Portal: pmmsy.dof.gov.in. NFDB Portal: nfdb.gov.in. Department of Fisheries Helpline: 1800-425-1660.

scheme_name: SVAMITVA Scheme (Survey of Villages and Mapping with Improvised Technology in Village Areas)
target_beneficiary: Rural property owners residing in populated (Abadi) village areas
benefit_details: Provides official legal Property Cards (Svamitva Card / Title Deed) to rural homeowners after high-resolution 3D drone mapping and ground demarcation by Survey of India. Enables rural citizens to use their home and village property as a financial asset to secure bank loans and credit.
eligibility_criteria: Residents possessing property in rural inhabited (Abadi) areas of notified survey villages across all participating states.
how_to_apply: No individual application needed. The Ministry of Panchayati Raj and Survey of India execute drone flights in coordination with the Gram Panchayat. Property claims and disputes are resolved via Gram Sabha before final card issuance.
documents_required: Aadhaar Card, local Gram Panchayat residence proof, existing village possession slips (if available).
contact_details: Portal: svamitva.nic.in. Ministry of Panchayati Raj. Contact local Gram Panchayat or Tehsil revenue officer.
